title: 2B agents are not copies of 2C: enterprises will let AI hack their systems
dek: The Afine founder believes 2C personal agents are oversaturated, competing on supply chains and subsidies; 2B agents more easily capture end-to-end value because bosses actively cooperate with AI to transform their companies.
why: A founder's retrospective from open-source document collaboration to enterprise agent transformation, with specific product judgments and training details—for those wanting to understand the evolution logic of the agent race.
who: Founders focused on agent product evolution, decision-makers building 2B enterprise software or AI transformation, and practitioners curious how model training lands in startups.
skip: The opening pleasantries about the founder's personal experiences can be skipped.

points.h: A hundred agents plus a hundred employees amplify noise
points.body: When you give each employee a Personal Agent, leadership no longer faces 100 employees but 100 employees plus 100 uncoordinated agents, amplifying noise rather than signal. Their solution is a single agent shared across the company with continuous learning that preserves individual memory and operating environments while learning across all business touchpoints.

points.h: 2C agents have almost no economies of scale
points.body: AI startups differ from internet startups because scale and network effects are greatly weakened—more users doesn't make your model smarter; the model's own intelligence improvement is decisive. This is why they don't build 2C personal agents: that market is about supply chains and subsidies, not product moats.

points.h: 2B bosses actively let AI hack their own systems
points.body: In C2C, getting all user information for recommendations is frightening; agents naturally need tricks and reverse engineering to get permissions. In B2B, when the boss sees that AI can trace end-to-end business data, financial data, and every code flow, the boss has strong incentive to actively transform systems to give AI more context. This makes 2B agents easier to adopt early on.

points.h: Workflow plugins have shorter and shorter lifespans
points.body: Products like LongChain, Dify, N8N, and Open Cloud that scaffolded workflows once soared in valuation but are barely mentioned by H2 2026. Not because better workflows replaced them, but because models absorbed these workflows—with smarter models, the first move is usually to delete previous skills and system prompts or they backfire. Determinism is shifting from outside the model to inside, through KV Cache and Prompt Cache hit rates.

points.h: Building your own models only became viable in 2026
points.body: The speaker deeply participated in training a domestic ET-scale multimodal agentic model and didn't believe startups could train models—big tech has vastly superior chips, talent density, and end-to-end infrastructure. But by 2026, with architecture changes (like Jamba models) and base model capabilities reaching threshold, small models don't need to beat AGI models; they just need to efficiently distill tasks they can definitely do at lower cost and faster latency. That makes startup model training viable.

points.h: Small models are the autonomic nervous system, large models are the cortex
points.body: They train two types of models. Task Routing Models distill the tool-calling patterns and user preferences from SOTA models into ‘muscle memory,’ letting small models form conditioned reflexes like learned bike riding. Worker Models of 20-40 billion parameters handle reverse-engineering and specific tasks at the operating-system level of enterprises, breaking through safety constraints. The intelligent large model is the cortex; their trained small models are the brainstem and spinal cord.

points.h: All software today is essentially open source
points.body: If anyone knows what your software does and can get the API spec, AI can reverse-engineer it or rewrite an identical replacement. So software itself is dying, and value shifts to model intelligence itself. The speaker predicts that in 2-3 years, open models will catch up much faster, AGI supply will become abundant, and the commercial rules for both B2B and C2C will change very bloodily.

points.h: Agents are crossing the inflection point that video once owned
points.body: In the past 2-3 years, only chat and video—with predictable delivery and commercial closure—made money early. General agents need end-to-end completion to create value; one missing step means zero value. But that gap recently closed, and the advantages video and companionship tracks accumulated face challenge from general infrastructure and general models. OPUS 5.5 is the best video-editing model, GPT6 Astra the best at robotic video control—a complete reversal.
